clue.text: Kind of pop music to make the joint jump?

parts.note: the hip is the joint at the top of the leg
to hop is to make a small jump

explanation.surface: A question about music that gets a nightclub bouncing.
explanation.walkthrough: The joint is also slang for a club, which the surface plays on.
explanation.definitionFit: This rap-based genre is a style of popular music born in New York.

clue.text: Tried drug, having to get over a bad trip

indicators.note: the drug word holds the other piece within it, so 'having' signals a container

parts.note: hash is short for hashish, a cannabis drug

indicators.note: turning over flips the words a and bad so they read right to left

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who tried a drug had to recover from a bad trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get over' turns the pair of words round (DABA), and the drug word is split after its second letter to hold them; 'trip' only completes the drug-taking picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a go at something is colloquially to have had a try at it, an idiom for attempted.

clue.text: Men on board made pledges

definitions.meaning: the smallest chess pieces on the board
left items with a broker as security for a loan, or vowed

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: chess pieces, and the past tense of handing goods over as security.

clue.text: Anything said by Northerner is inaccurate

indicators.note: a northern English speaker says this dialect word, which a southerner hears as a different word

parts.note: owt is northern English dialect for anything

explanation.surface: Whatever a man from the North says is wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: OWT is northern English dialect for 'anything' (and NOWT for 'nothing').
explanation.definitionFit: A guess that is wide of the mark is said to be off, a common idiom for being wrong.

clue.text: Composer daily consuming cheese

indicators.note: eating something takes it inside, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a daily is a cleaner who comes in by the day, also called a char or charwoman (British)
brie is a soft French cheese

explanation.surface: A composer eats cheese every day.
explanation.walkthrough: A daily in Britain is a cleaning woman, a char.
explanation.definitionFit: Emmanuel Chabrier was a French composer, best known for the rhapsody Espana.

clue.text: Top ten potential victims?

definitions.meaning: a chart of the most popular records, a list of hits
a list of people marked out for killing by a gangster

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both a pop chart of best-selling songs and a gangster's roll of intended targets.

clue.text: Something for graduate to make notes on that's flat

parts.note: a bachelor is the holder of a first university degree
a pad of paper is something to jot notes on

explanation.surface: A notebook for a university graduate turns out to be a flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Something for graduate' and 'to make notes on' together paint a writing pad for a student.
explanation.definitionFit: A single man's apartment, informally called this, is a kind of flat.

clue.text: Little rascal, very energetic, making a strong impression

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous child
active means lively and full of energy

explanation.surface: A lively small child makes quite an impact on people.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes something that strikes forcefully, related to impact.

clue.text: Set another examination round about half term holiday

indicators.note: the holiday word goes round the other piece, wrapping it

parts.note: a rest is a break or holiday

indicators.note: the first half of the word term is taken

explanation.surface: A teacher sets a fresh exam around the half-term break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round about' reads like a vague 'approximately', but it is the container signal; 'half' takes the first two letters of 'term'.
explanation.definitionFit: To examine again is to test a second time, so the verb means set a new examination.

clue.text: No teacher has a grasp of English? That's rather curious

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the teacher word holds the other letter in its grasp, enclosing it

parts.note: pupils address a male teacher as sir

explanation.surface: A teacher who can't speak English raises eyebrows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has a grasp of' reads as knowing a language, but it signals the letter going inside the teacher word.
explanation.definitionFit: The comparative of a word meaning inquisitive, so it means more prying than usual.

clue.text: Fail to enjoy party before comedian entertains you

indicators.note: the party word comes before the rest in the answer

parts.note: a do is a party or social event

indicators.note: to entertain a guest is to have them inside, so one piece holds another

parts.note: a wit is a clever, funny person
thou is an old form of you

explanation.surface: Someone misses out on the fun at a party where a comedian performs for you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertains' signals a container: the old pronoun splits the comedian word after its second letter; 'before' puts the party first.
explanation.definitionFit: To go without something is to forgo it, so you fail to have or enjoy it.

clue.text: Look out for member of aircrew, and get into trouble

indicators.note: the word for look is taken out of the crew member

parts.note: a copilot is the second pilot on the flight deck
lo is an old word meaning look or behold

explanation.surface: Watch out for the airline crew, or you'll be in trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Look out' looks like the phrase 'watch out'; really LO is removed from COPILOT.
explanation.definitionFit: This British slang idiom means to be punished or land in serious trouble.

clue.text: Food of possibly Semitic and Arab origin

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters may be arranged in another way

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dish that may come from the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges the letters of SEMITIC and ARAB together.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-grain rice from South Asia is a staple food.

clue.text: Is grateful for fresh pasta recipe

indicators.note: fresh suggests something new, so the letters are made into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone thanks the cook for a new pasta recipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fresh' rearranges the letters of PASTA and RECIPE.
explanation.definitionFit: To value or be thankful for something is a standard sense of the verb.

clue.text: Lettuce in tabasco sauce?

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the words tabasco sauce

explanation.surface: A salad leaf tossed in hot pepper sauce?
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to the letters across the gap in 'tabasCO Sauce'.
explanation.definitionFit: Romaine lettuce is also known by this name, after the Greek island.

clue.text: One buying and selling?

definitions.meaning: someone who informs on another, selling them out to the police (British slang)

explanation.definitionFit: The noun is both a customer and, in British slang, an informer who betrays someone.

clue.text: Attack old actor's last three parts being the lead?

indicators.text: last three parts being the lead
indicators.note: the final three letters move to the front, taking the lead

parts.note: Charles Laughton was a mid-20th-century British actor

explanation.surface: A veteran actor's final roles in the leading part come under fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last three parts being the lead' takes ONS from the end of LAUGHTON'S and puts it at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: A fierce, overwhelming assault is a synonym for an attack.

clue.text: Admitted having cheated

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both received someone in and conned or fooled them.

clue.text: Drink frequently swallowed to break down resistance

indicators.note: the drink word swallows the other, taking it inside

parts.note: to sup is to drink
often means frequently

explanation.surface: Downing a drink often weakens your defences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swallowed' fits the drinking picture but signals the frequency word going inside the drink word.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to weaken someone's opposition before persuading them.

clue.text: A source of sherry and a source of water also

indicators.note: the source or start of sherry is its first letter

parts.note: a well is a source of water

explanation.surface: A list of where to get sherry and where to get water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A source of sherry' gives A and S, then a well is a source of water.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in addition, so it is a synonym for too.

clue.text: Lazy person, one enrolled by education authority, had teaching diploma

indicators.note: one is enrolled by the authority, put inside it

parts.note: LEA is a Local Education Authority in Britain
I is the Roman numeral one
BEd is a Bachelor of Education, a teaching qualification

explanation.surface: A slacker joins the council's education department, armed with a teaching diploma.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enrolled by' puts I inside LEA, a British Local Education Authority.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who stays in bed late is a lazy person, a slugabed.

clue.text: Top dog, one hunted endlessly in oriental sport

indicators.note: the shortened word goes in the sport word

parts.note: sumo is Japanese wrestling

indicators.note: the last letter of the word for one hunted is removed

parts.note: prey is an animal hunted by others

explanation.surface: The champion is chased relentlessly in a Japanese sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops the last letter of the hunted word; 'in' puts what is left inside the Japanese wrestling word.
explanation.definitionFit: A boss or leader is a top dog, an idiom for the person in charge.

clue.text: Private theatre starting to prosper, since being taken over

indicators.note: taken over means turned upside down, so in a down light the letters read upwards

parts.note: rep is repertory theatre

indicators.note: the first letter of prosper is taken

parts.note: as means since or because

explanation.surface: A private theatre begins to thrive after a takeover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being taken over' turns the whole run of theatre, P and since round to read upwards. 'Private' is a noun: the Royal Engineers' rank for a private soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: A sapper is the rank of private soldier in the British Royal Engineers.

clue.text: A sore point? Give us a ring

definitions.meaning: a patch of hard, thick skin that may be tender

explanation.definitionFit: A hardened patch of skin is a callosity; the phrase split up is a request to phone.

clue.text: Expression of surprise finding pathway regularly obscured

indicators.note: every other letter is obscured, leaving the alternate ones

explanation.surface: Someone is surprised to find a path periodically blocked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly obscured' hides P, T, W and Y in 'pathway'.
explanation.definitionFit: This interjection is an exclamation of discovery or surprise.

clue.text: One in deep trouble to be brought in next? Unwise

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: to trouble something is to stir it up, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone in deep trouble being called next would be ill-advised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' rearranges I, IN and DEEP, with NEXT also 'brought in' to the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Not advisable or practical in the circumstances, so a synonym for imprudent.

clue.text: Young swimmer, one going deeper having removed cap

indicators.note: the cap of a down word is its top, so the first letter is removed

parts.note: a delver is someone who digs deep

explanation.surface: A youngster in the pool, diving deeper, has lost their swimming cap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having removed cap' takes off the D of DELVER.
explanation.definitionFit: A young eel is called an elver, a small swimming fish.

clue.text: Right, scarper!

definitions.meaning: British slang for run away fast

explanation.definitionFit: Informal for lawful or genuine; split in two it is slang for running off.

clue.text: Make neither profit nor loss from holiday flat

parts.note: a break is a short holiday
even means flat or level

explanation.surface: A business just covers the cost of a holiday apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' looks like an apartment but means level.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means to finish with income exactly matching costs.

clue.text: Stun one fish?

parts.note: KO is a knockout, stunning a boxer
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A question of how to stun a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A koi is an ornamental Japanese carp.

clue.text: Reserve assigned to a team

parts.note: set means assigned, as a task is set
taken as written
a side is a team

explanation.surface: A substitute is assigned to a team.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reserve' is a verb here: to keep back.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep something back for later use is to put it by, the same as reserving it.

clue.text: Military report put forward is rejected

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the words read backwards

parts.note: pert means forward or cheeky
taken as written

explanation.surface: A military report put forward is turned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put' is a link: PERT (forward) plus IS, both turned back.
explanation.definitionFit: This is short for situation report, a military term for an update on conditions.
